about: Château Meyney is one of the oldest wine estates in Saint-Estèphe. Its vines were first planted by monks in the Middle Ages, and the Feuillant order built the estate house in 1662. The négociant Désiré Cordier bought it in 1919 and added Petit Verdot in the 1920s, and that grape is still part of Meyney’s character. The 51-hectare vineyard is a single block on a rise overlooking the Gironde, next to Château Montrose. Since 2004 it has been owned by the Crédit Agricole group.

Meyney’s gravel soils sit over clay and limestone, with a deep vein of blue clay like the one under Pétrus that holds water for the vines. The estate is planted to about half Cabernet Sauvignon, a third Merlot and 15% Petit Verdot. Grapes are sorted in the vineyard and again by hand at the winery, each plot is fermented separately in steel or concrete vats, and the wine is aged 12 to 18 months in French oak, about a third of it new.

2010 was a great Bordeaux vintage, ripe and structured, and Meyney made one of its best wines of the decade. Robert Parker’s Wine Advocate called it a sleeper of the vintage and noted black currant, graphite and savoury, meaty notes in a full-bodied, concentrated wine built to age. After fifteen years the tannins have softened, and the wine now pairs fresh fruit with a firm, dense structure.
facts: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot (estate plantings about 50/35/15)
12–18 months in French oak, about one-third new (estate practice)
